title: Gatineau police say 911 protocol not followed in Gauvreau homicide
subtitle: Thérèse Gauvreau, 83, found dead at home on Boulevard de la Cité-des-jeunes on Jan. 18
article: A preliminary investigation by Gatineau police found the 911 operator who took the call related to 83-year-old Thérèse Gauvreau's homicide did not follow proper protocol, leading to a 30-minute delay in the response.

Police said the operator at the emergency call centre did not properly assess the urgency of the call, which involved reports of an agitated man acting suspiciously on Boulevard de la Cité-des-jeunes around noon Jan. 18.
Gatineau police Chief Mario Harel spoke to reporters after speaking to Gatineau's mayor and councillors.
"It was unacceptable, the call was mishandled and we will correct this," Harel said in French.
According to the preliminary investigation, no patrol vehicle was available to respond, but Harel said one should have been made available given the severity of the call.
Harel said if the call were handled properly, officers would've arrived on the scene sooner, but he could not say how much or whether it could have saved Gauvreau's life.
"This is a very hypothetical question that I don't have the information to respond to that," Harel said.
Officers arrived on the scene half an hour after the initial call from a neighbour. They found the suspect behind 171 Boul. de la Cité-des-jeunes. Soon after, they found Gauvreau's body.
Jean-François Dupuis, 21, has been charged with second-degree murder.
Police said administrative measures have been taken against the 911 operator, but will not comment on the details.
In light of this case, Gatineau police will be conducting an analysis on the management of emergency calls.
Gatineau Mayor Maxime Pedneaud-Jobin said council asked police to not just analyze the specific situation but provide a "diagnostic" report on whether there are larger problems with the 911 system.
"I don't think we have any evidence to suggest a systemic problem, but we have to check anyway. That's what council asked for. We don't want any risk in the system," he said in French.
Councillor Louise Boudrais had proposed an external investigation into how police handled the call, but it did not receive the support of council or the mayor.
"It's not necessary. We have confidence in our chief of police," Pedneaud-Jobin said.
Harel said police will look at how recruitment, training and current operating procedures should be changed to improve the emergency dispatch system.
The report will be delivered to the municipal public safety and traffic commission in May.
